title: Why Are We Sometimes So Wrong About Who Has Extraordinary Talent
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article catalogs the famous early rejections of now-legendary figures, Fred Astaire, Tom Brady, Walt Disney, Oprah Winfrey, Steven Spielberg, Paul McCartney, and J.K. Rowling, to explore why talent scouts and evaluators so often miss future greatness. The author argues that the missing variable isn't talent but drive, an intangible quality that resists reliable assessment and, in some cases, doesn't even fully ignite until after rejection or failure. Rather than lamenting the inevitability of missed evaluations, the piece encourages readers to watch closely for the unmistakable signs of relentless commitment to self-improvement, since that is the real predictor of eventual greatness.
points: Many legendary figures, from Fred Astaire to Oprah Winfrey to J.K. Rowling, were dismissed early as lacking talent.
Evaluators consistently miss future greatness because they focus on measurable skill rather than drive.
Drive is an intangible quality that is difficult to assess and sometimes doesn't emerge until after failure.
It's often the extraordinary commitment to self-improvement, not raw talent, that produces exceptional performers.
Missing some future stars during evaluation is inevitable, but recognizing drive when you see it is the real skill.
quotes: Many of the greatest performers of all time, across multiple fields and disciplines, were once judged as having little or no talent.
One talent scout’s assessment of acclaimed dancer Fred Astaire read: “Can’t act, slightly bald; can dance a little.
Walt Disney was once dismissed from a newspaper job because he lacked creativity and failed to generate original ideas.
Of all the predictors, indicators, and barometers employed through assessments of talent, the one intangible quality that can never be accurately diagnosed or identified is drive.
People who are willing to do whatever it takes and never let the foot off the pedal of self-improvement develop extreme talents and skills and not the other way around.
For those who have found a spark that has turned into a flame there is no time off from the work at becoming great.
